### Problem: Working out {#sec-gd-p1-work}

::: {.p-statement}
A gym is an $n \times m$ grid. Working out in cell $(i, j)$ burns $a[i][j]$ calories. Iahub starts at the top-left and must finish at the bottom-right, moving only right or down. Iahubina starts at the bottom-left and must finish at the top-right, moving only right or up. Their paths meet in exactly one cell, and at that cell neither of them works out. Every other cell on either path is worked out once. Maximise the total calories.

$3 \le n, m \le 1000$ and $0 \le a[i][j] \le 10^5$. On a $3 \times 3$ of 100s with a 1 in the centre the answer is 800.

Source: [CF 429B · Working out](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/429/B){.solved rating="1600"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
"Let Iahub take a best path, then give Iahubina her best path that meets it once" loses. On

$$
\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 7 & 1 & 5 \\ 5 & 1 & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 8 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Iahub's best path alone is worth 25 and takes the 7, the 6, and the 8. Iahubina then has one place to cross it, and the best total of that kind is 33. The optimum is 40: Iahub gives up the 6 and they cross on the cheap cell of value 1. The two people interact only through the meeting cell, so the cell is chosen first and each route is optimised around it.

They meet at $X = (i, j)$. Each route splits into a half before $X$ and a half after $X$. That is four right/down or right/up paths, one from each corner:

- $d_1[i][j]$: best sum from the top-left to $(i, j)$, right or down;
- $d_2[i][j]$: best sum from $(i, j)$ to the bottom-right, right or down;
- $d_3[i][j]$: best sum from the bottom-left to $(i, j)$, right or up;
- $d_4[i][j]$: best sum from $(i, j)$ to the top-right, right or up.

Each table includes $a$ at both of its own ends. Iahub enters $X$ from above or from the left and leaves down or right. Iahubina enters from below or from the left and leaves up or right. If they used a common neighbour they would meet twice. Of the 16 local combinations, two survive. In crossing A, Iahub goes left to right and Iahubina goes below to up. In crossing B, Iahub goes above to below and Iahubina goes left to right.

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(i, j) &= d_1[i][j-1] + d_2[i][j+1] + d_3[i+1][j] + d_4[i-1][j],\\
B(i, j) &= d_1[i-1][j] + d_2[i+1][j] + d_3[i][j-1] + d_4[i][j+1].
\end{aligned}
$$

The answer is the maximum of $A$ and $B$ over interior cells. The cell $(i, j)$ is never added: every table is read at a neighbour. Both crossings use all four neighbours, so a border cell cannot be the meeting. The loops run over $1 \le i \le n-2$ and $1 \le j \le m-2$ in 0-based indices, which is also why every $i \pm 1$ and $j \pm 1$ is inside the grid.

On the $3 \times 4$ example the only interior cells are $(1, 1)$ and $(1, 2)$. Crossing A at $(1, 1)$ is $7 + 15 + 4 + 13 = 39$. Crossing B there is $9 + 12 + 6 + 13 = 40$. Crossing B at $(1, 2)$ is the greedy 33. The four numbers in the winning sum are the two people's halves, and the 1 on the meeting cell is in none of them.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **States.** Four tables $d_1..d_4$, each including $a$ at both ends of its own path.
- **Transitions.** $d_1[i][j] = a[i][j] + \max(d_1[i-1][j], d_1[i][j-1])$. $d_2$ reads down and right. $d_3$ reads down and left. $d_4$ reads up and right.
- **Base.** Each table's own corner holds $a$ of that corner. A missing neighbour contributes $-\infty$. Because $a \ge 0$, a 0 in the padding is the same fact.
- **Orders.** $d_1$ rows downward, columns rightward. $d_2$ rows upward, columns leftward. $d_3$ rows upward, columns rightward. $d_4$ rows downward, columns leftward.
- **Answer.** The better of crossings A and B over every interior cell. **Cost.** $O(nm)$ time and four tables. A half-path has at most 1999 cells, so one entry is at most about $2 \cdot 10^8$ and four of them about $8 \cdot 10^8$, inside a 32-bit integer. The sum of four entries wants a 64-bit temporary.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
Each corner is a suffix or a prefix, the same shape as minimum path sum with a maximum. `d1(i, j)` is the best sum from the top-left to `(i, j)`, both ends included. The other three functions differ in the corner and in the two neighbours they read. Both crossings are then evaluated at every interior cell. The meeting cell is not one of the four reads.
:::

##### Python

```{python}
def work_rec(a):
    n, m = len(a), len(a[0])

    def d1(i, j):
        if i == 0 and j == 0:
            return a[0][0]
        best = 0
        if i:
            best = max(best, d1(i - 1, j))
        if j:
            best = max(best, d1(i, j - 1))
        return a[i][j] + best

    def d2(i, j):
        if i == n - 1 and j == m - 1:
            return a[i][j]
        best = 0
        if i + 1 < n:
            best = max(best, d2(i + 1, j))
        if j + 1 < m:
            best = max(best, d2(i, j + 1))
        return a[i][j] + best

    def d3(i, j):
        if i == n - 1 and j == 0:
            return a[i][j]
        best = 0
        if i + 1 < n:
            best = max(best, d3(i + 1, j))
        if j:
            best = max(best, d3(i, j - 1))
        return a[i][j] + best

    def d4(i, j):
        if i == 0 and j == m - 1:
            return a[i][j]
        best = 0
        if i:
            best = max(best, d4(i - 1, j))
        if j + 1 < m:
            best = max(best, d4(i, j + 1))
        return a[i][j] + best

    best = 0
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        for j in range(1, m - 1):
            A = d1(i, j - 1) + d2(i, j + 1) + d3(i + 1, j) + d4(i - 1, j)
            B = d1(i - 1, j) + d2(i + 1, j) + d3(i, j - 1) + d4(i, j + 1)
            best = max(best, A, B)
    return best
```

```cpp
    if (i == 0 && j == 0) return a[0][0];
    long long best = 0;
    if (i) best = max(best, d1Work(i - 1, j, a));
    if (j) best = max(best, d1Work(i, j - 1, a));
    return a[i][j] + best;
}
long long d2Work(int i, int j, const vector<vector<int>>& a) {
    int n = a.size(), m = a[0].size();
    if (i == n - 1 && j == m - 1) return a[i][j];
    long long best = 0;
    if (i + 1 < n) best = max(best, d2Work(i + 1, j, a));
    if (j + 1 < m) best = max(best, d2Work(i, j + 1, a));
    return a[i][j] + best;
}
long long d3Work(int i, int j, const vector<vector<int>>& a) {
    int n = a.size();
    if (i == n - 1 && j == 0) return a[i][j];
    long long best = 0;
    if (i + 1 < n) best = max(best, d3Work(i + 1, j, a));
    if (j) best = max(best, d3Work(i, j - 1, a));
    return a[i][j] + best;
}
long long d4Work(int i, int j, const vector<vector<int>>& a) {
    int m = a[0].size();
    if (i == 0 && j == m - 1) return a[i][j];
    long long best = 0;
    if (i) best = max(best, d4Work(i - 1, j, a));
    if (j + 1 < m) best = max(best, d4Work(i, j + 1, a));
    return a[i][j] + best;
}
long long workRec(const vector<vector<int>>& a) {
    int n = a.size(), m = a[0].size();
    long long best = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < n - 1; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j < m - 1; ++j) {
            long long A = d1Work(i, j - 1, a) + d2Work(i, j + 1, a) + d3Work(i + 1, j, a) + d4Work(i - 1, j, a);
            long long B = d1Work(i - 1, j, a) + d2Work(i + 1, j, a) + d3Work(i, j - 1, a) + d4Work(i, j + 1, a);
            best = max(best, max(A, B));
        }
    return best;
}
```

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
Each corner has $nm$ calls. Store them. The values are non-negative, so $-1$ means "not computed yet". The body is the previous button. The four arrays in front of the recursive calls are the new lines. The combination is unchanged: it still reads neighbours, and it still skips the meeting cell.
:::

```{python}
def work_memo(a):
    n, m = len(a), len(a[0])
    m1 = [[-1] * m for _ in range(n)]
    m2 = [[-1] * m for _ in range(n)]
    m3 = [[-1] * m for _ in range(n)]
    m4 = [[-1] * m for _ in range(n)]

    def d1(i, j):
        if m1[i][j] >= 0:
            return m1[i][j]
        if i == 0 and j == 0:
            m1[i][j] = a[0][0]
            return m1[i][j]
        best = 0
        if i:
            best = max(best, d1(i - 1, j))
        if j:
            best = max(best, d1(i, j - 1))
        m1[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
        return m1[i][j]

    def d2(i, j):
        if m2[i][j] >= 0:
            return m2[i][j]
        if i == n - 1 and j == m - 1:
            m2[i][j] = a[i][j]
            return m2[i][j]
        best = 0
        if i + 1 < n:
            best = max(best, d2(i + 1, j))
        if j + 1 < m:
            best = max(best, d2(i, j + 1))
        m2[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
        return m2[i][j]

    def d3(i, j):
        if m3[i][j] >= 0:
            return m3[i][j]
        if i == n - 1 and j == 0:
            m3[i][j] = a[i][j]
            return m3[i][j]
        best = 0
        if i + 1 < n:
            best = max(best, d3(i + 1, j))
        if j:
            best = max(best, d3(i, j - 1))
        m3[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
        return m3[i][j]

    def d4(i, j):
        if m4[i][j] >= 0:
            return m4[i][j]
        if i == 0 and j == m - 1:
            m4[i][j] = a[i][j]
            return m4[i][j]
        best = 0
        if i:
            best = max(best, d4(i - 1, j))
        if j + 1 < m:
            best = max(best, d4(i, j + 1))
        m4[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
        return m4[i][j]

    best = 0
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        for j in range(1, m - 1):
            A = d1(i, j - 1) + d2(i, j + 1) + d3(i + 1, j) + d4(i - 1, j)
            B = d1(i - 1, j) + d2(i + 1, j) + d3(i, j - 1) + d4(i, j + 1)
            best = max(best, A, B)
    return best
```

#### Four tables

::: {.form-next}
The calls go away. Each table is filled from its own corner, in the direction its two neighbours already lie. $d_3$ walks upward and rightward: it comes from the bottom-left. $d_4$ walks downward and leftward: it comes from the top-right. Mixing those directions reads zeros. The combination is the same two crossings.
:::

```{python}
def work_tables(a):
    n, m = len(a), len(a[0])
    neg = -(10**18)
    d1 = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    d2 = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    d3 = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    d4 = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(m):
            best = 0 if (i, j) == (0, 0) else neg
            if i:
                best = max(best, d1[i - 1][j])
            if j:
                best = max(best, d1[i][j - 1])
            if (i, j) == (0, 0):
                best = 0
            d1[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        for j in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            best = 0 if (i, j) == (n - 1, m - 1) else neg
            if i + 1 < n:
                best = max(best, d2[i + 1][j])
            if j + 1 < m:
                best = max(best, d2[i][j + 1])
            if (i, j) == (n - 1, m - 1):
                best = 0
            d2[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        for j in range(m):
            best = 0 if (i, j) == (n - 1, 0) else neg
            if i + 1 < n:
                best = max(best, d3[i + 1][j])
            if j:
                best = max(best, d3[i][j - 1])
            if (i, j) == (n - 1, 0):
                best = 0
            d3[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            best = 0 if (i, j) == (0, m - 1) else neg
            if i:
                best = max(best, d4[i - 1][j])
            if j + 1 < m:
                best = max(best, d4[i][j + 1])
            if (i, j) == (0, m - 1):
                best = 0
            d4[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
    return d1, d2, d3, d4

def work_tab(a):
    n, m = len(a), len(a[0])
    d1, d2, d3, d4 = work_tables(a)
    best = 0
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        for j in range(1, m - 1):
            A = d1[i][j - 1] + d2[i][j + 1] + d3[i + 1][j] + d4[i - 1][j]
            B = d1[i - 1][j] + d2[i + 1][j] + d3[i][j - 1] + d4[i][j + 1]
            best = max(best, A, B)
    return best
```

##### C++

```cpp
long long workTab(const vector<vector<int>>& a) {
    int n = a.size(), m = a[0].size();
    const long long NEG = -(1LL << 60);
    vector<vector<long long>> d1(n, vector<long long>(m)), d2 = d1, d3 = d1, d4 = d1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        for (int j = 0; j < m; ++j) {
            long long best = (i == 0 && j == 0) ? 0 : NEG;
            if (i) best = max(best, d1[i - 1][j]);
            if (j) best = max(best, d1[i][j - 1]);
            if (i == 0 && j == 0) best = 0;
            d1[i][j] = a[i][j] + best;
        }
    for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i)
        for (int j = m - 1; j >= 0; --j) {
            long long best = (i == n - 1 && j == m - 1) ? 0 : NEG;
            if (i + 1 < n) best = max(best, d2[i + 1][j]);
            if (j + 1 < m) best = max(best, d2[i][j + 1]);
            if (i == n - 1 && j == m - 1) best = 0;
            d2[i][j] = a[i][j] + best;
        }
    for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i)
        for (int j = 0; j < m; ++j) {
            long long best = (i == n - 1 && j == 0) ? 0 : NEG;
            if (i + 1 < n) best = max(best, d3[i + 1][j]);
            if (j) best = max(best, d3[i][j - 1]);
            if (i == n - 1 && j == 0) best = 0;
            d3[i][j] = a[i][j] + best;
        }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        for (int j = m - 1; j >= 0; --j) {
            long long best = (i == 0 && j == m - 1) ? 0 : NEG;
            if (i) best = max(best, d4[i - 1][j]);
            if (j + 1 < m) best = max(best, d4[i][j + 1]);
            if (i == 0 && j == m - 1) best = 0;
            d4[i][j] = a[i][j] + best;
        }
    long long best = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < n - 1; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j < m - 1; ++j) {
            long long A = d1[i][j - 1] + d2[i][j + 1] + d3[i + 1][j] + d4[i - 1][j];
            long long B = d1[i - 1][j] + d2[i + 1][j] + d3[i][j - 1] + d4[i][j + 1];
            best = max(best, max(A, B));
        }
    return best;
}
```

:::

#### Rolled rows

::: {.form-next}
The combination at row `i` reads $d_1$ and $d_4$ only on rows `i - 1` and `i`, and $d_2$ and $d_3$ on rows `i` and `i + 1`. The top-down tables can be built during one downward sweep, two rows each. The bottom-up tables run against that sweep, so they are finished first and kept in full. Whichever way the sweep goes, two of the four tables run against it.
:::

```{python}
def work_meet(a):
    n, m = len(a), len(a[0])
    neg = -(10**18)
    d2 = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    d3 = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        for j in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            best = 0 if (i, j) == (n - 1, m - 1) else neg
            if i + 1 < n:
                best = max(best, d2[i + 1][j])
            if j + 1 < m:
                best = max(best, d2[i][j + 1])
            if (i, j) == (n - 1, m - 1):
                best = 0
            d2[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
        for j in range(m):
            best = 0 if (i, j) == (n - 1, 0) else neg
            if i + 1 < n:
                best = max(best, d3[i + 1][j])
            if j:
                best = max(best, d3[i][j - 1])
            if (i, j) == (n - 1, 0):
                best = 0
            d3[i][j] = a[i][j] + best
    p1 = [0] * m
    p4 = [0] * m
    best = 0
    for i in range(n):
        c1 = [0] * m
        c4 = [0] * m
        for j in range(m):
            prev = 0 if (i, j) == (0, 0) else neg
            if i:
                prev = max(prev, p1[j])
            if j:
                prev = max(prev, c1[j - 1])
            if (i, j) == (0, 0):
                prev = 0
            c1[j] = a[i][j] + prev
        for j in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            prev = 0 if (i, j) == (0, m - 1) else neg
            if i:
                prev = max(prev, p4[j])
            if j + 1 < m:
                prev = max(prev, c4[j + 1])
            if (i, j) == (0, m - 1):
                prev = 0
            c4[j] = a[i][j] + prev
        if 0 < i < n - 1:
            for j in range(1, m - 1):
                A = c1[j - 1] + d2[i][j + 1] + d3[i + 1][j] + p4[j]
                B = p1[j] + d2[i + 1][j] + d3[i][j - 1] + c4[j + 1]
                best = max(best, A, B)
        p1, p4 = c1, c4
    return best

def _monotone(n, m, sr, sc, gr, gc, moves):
    out = []

    def rec(r, c, path):
        if (r, c) == (gr, gc):
            out.append(list(path))
            return
        for dr, dc in moves:
            nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
            if 0 <= nr < n and 0 <= nc < m:
                path.append((nr, nc))
                rec(nr, nc, path)
                path.pop()

    rec(sr, sc, [(sr, sc)])
    return out

def greedy_then_other(a):
    """Iahub keeps one maximum path. Iahubina then takes her best path that meets it once."""
    n, m = len(a), len(a[0])
    iahub = _monotone(n, m, 0, 0, n - 1, m - 1, ((1, 0), (0, 1)))
    other = _monotone(n, m, n - 1, 0, 0, m - 1, ((-1, 0), (0, 1)))
    solo = max(sum(a[r][c] for r, c in path) for path in iahub)
    best = 0
    for path in iahub:
        if sum(a[r][c] for r, c in path) != solo:
            continue
        cells = set(path)
        for q in other:
            inter = cells & set(q)
            if len(inter) != 1:
                continue
            cell = next(iter(inter))
            total = sum(a[r][c] for r, c in path) + sum(a[r][c] for r, c in q) - 2 * a[cell[0]][cell[1]]
            best = max(best, total)
    return best, solo

_gym = [[100, 100, 100], [100, 1, 100], [100, 100, 100]]
_ex = [[2, 7, 1, 5], [5, 1, 6, 2], [1, 3, 8, 1]]
assert work_rec(_gym) == work_memo(_gym) == work_tab(_gym) == work_meet(_gym) == 800
assert work_rec(_ex) == work_memo(_ex) == work_tab(_ex) == work_meet(_ex) == 40
_greedy, _solo = greedy_then_other(_ex)
assert _solo == 25 and _greedy == 33
_d1, _d2, _d3, _d4 = work_tables(_ex)
assert _d1[0][1] + _d2[2][1] + _d3[1][0] + _d4[1][2] == 40
assert _d1[1][0] + _d2[1][2] + _d3[2][1] + _d4[0][1] == 39
_iahub = {(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1), (2, 2), (2, 3)}
_ina = {(2, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3), (0, 3)}
assert _iahub & _ina == {(1, 1)}
assert sum(_ex[r][c] for r, c in _iahub | _ina) - _ex[1][1] == 40
assert _ex[1][1] == 1
```

##### C++

```cpp
long long workMeet(const vector<vector<int>>& a) {
    int n = a.size(), m = a[0].size();
    const long long NEG = -(1LL << 60);
    vector<vector<long long>> d2(n, vector<long long>(m)), d3 = d2;
    for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i) {
        for (int j = m - 1; j >= 0; --j) {
            long long best = (i == n - 1 && j == m - 1) ? 0 : NEG;
            if (i + 1 < n) best = max(best, d2[i + 1][j]);
            if (j + 1 < m) best = max(best, d2[i][j + 1]);
            if (i == n - 1 && j == m - 1) best = 0;
            d2[i][j] = a[i][j] + best;
        }
        for (int j = 0; j < m; ++j) {
            long long best = (i == n - 1 && j == 0) ? 0 : NEG;
            if (i + 1 < n) best = max(best, d3[i + 1][j]);
            if (j) best = max(best, d3[i][j - 1]);
            if (i == n - 1 && j == 0) best = 0;
            d3[i][j] = a[i][j] + best;
        }
    }
    vector<long long> p1(m), c1(m), p4(m), c4(m);
    long long best = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        for (int j = 0; j < m; ++j) {
            long long prev = (i == 0 && j == 0) ? 0 : NEG;
            if (i) prev = max(prev, p1[j]);
            if (j) prev = max(prev, c1[j - 1]);
            if (i == 0 && j == 0) prev = 0;
            c1[j] = a[i][j] + prev;
        }
        for (int j = m - 1; j >= 0; --j) {
            long long prev = (i == 0 && j == m - 1) ? 0 : NEG;
            if (i) prev = max(prev, p4[j]);
            if (j + 1 < m) prev = max(prev, c4[j + 1]);
            if (i == 0 && j == m - 1) prev = 0;
            c4[j] = a[i][j] + prev;
        }
        if (i > 0 && i + 1 < n)
            for (int j = 1; j + 1 < m; ++j) {
                long long A = c1[j - 1] + d2[i][j + 1] + d3[i + 1][j] + p4[j];
                long long B = p1[j] + d2[i + 1][j] + d3[i][j - 1] + c4[j + 1];
                best = max(best, max(A, B));
            }
        swap(p1, c1);
        swap(p4, c4);
    }
    return best;
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** recomputes every corner. On these grids it is a few thousand calls; the same functions on $1000 \times 1000$ do not finish. **Memoisation** is $O(nm)$ states and $O(1)$ work per state, plus a stack of length at most $n + m$. **Four tables** are $O(nm)$ time and four grids. **Rolled rows** are the same time and two full tables plus $O(m)$: $d_2$ and $d_3$ stay, $d_1$ and $d_4$ are two live rows.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- The official $3 \times 3$ has one interior cell. Both crossings read four neighbours of 200, and $4 \cdot 200 = 800$. The centre 1 is not in the sum.
- On the $3 \times 4$ example, crossing A alone reaches 39 and crossing B reaches 40. One crossing is the wrong program.
- A border cell has no legal crossing. The loops start at index 1 and stop before the last row and the last column.
- Iahub's best path on the $3 \times 4$ example is worth 25. Forcing Iahubina to cross that path once is worth 33.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Adding the meeting cell, or reading the tables at the meeting cell, counts $a[i][j]$ several times. The statement counts it zero times. Read each table at the neighbour that person uses.
- Trying only "Iahub horizontal, Iahubina vertical" misses the better crossing. On the $3 \times 4$ example that is 39 against 40.
- A loop over the whole grid reads $i \pm 1$ or $j \pm 1$ off the board. Zero padding does not crash, and it invents routes that meet twice or skip a corner. The samples can still pass.
- $d_3$ is filled upward, columns left to right. $d_4$ is filled downward, columns right to left. The official sample is symmetric and hides a swapped direction. The $3 \times 4$ example does not.
:::

**Variants.** [LC 764 · Largest Plus Sign](https://leetcode.com/problems/largest-plus-sign/){difficulty="Medium"} is four arms of ones meeting at a centre: one running length from each side, and the answer is the best $\min$ of the four arms. [CF 1555C · Coin Rows](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1555/C){rating="1300"} is the same "meet at a column" idea on a $2 \times m$ grid. Alice turns down in one column, and Bob is left with a suffix of the top row or a prefix of the bottom row. [LC 2245 · Maximum Trailing Zeros in a Cornered Path](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-trailing-zeros-in-a-cornered-path/){difficulty="Medium"} joins a horizontal arm and a vertical arm at one turning cell, after prefix counts of the factors 2 and 5. [LC 2556 · Disconnect Path in a Binary Matrix by at Most One Flip](https://leetcode.com/problems/disconnect-path-in-a-binary-matrix-by-at-most-one-flip/){difficulty="Medium"} asks whether one cell lies on every right/down path: the forward and backward reachability tables, and an anti-diagonal that has a single cell on some path.

::: {.practice}
- [CF 1555C · Coin Rows](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1555/C){rating="1300"}
- Cells on some optimal path. A cell $X$ is on a maximum path when $f[X] + b[X] - a[X]$ equals the optimum. On $[[2, 7, 1, 5], [5, 1, 6, 2], [1, 3, 8, 1]]$ that count is 7.
:::
